title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) C: Lens modelling pipeline overview
comment: 29 pages, 16 figures. Submitted to A&A. Catalogue: https://euclid-eclipse-lenses.org ; data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19654904
summary: Galaxy-scale strong lenses provide precise measurements of galaxy mass distributions, magnified views of distant galaxies, and a competitive cosmological probe. Historically, such studies have been limited to hundreds of lenses, with automated modelling methods proving difficult to scale. We present automated lens modelling of 15 072 strong-lens candidates from Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), over an order of magnitude larger than any previously modelled sample. Using PyAutoLens-JAX, we perform three fits with multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE), pixelised, and Sérsic representations of the source, adopting an isothermal ellipsoid mass model with external shear. These fits provide foreground lens-light subtraction, adaptive Delaunay source reconstructions, and deblended photometry. More than 20 expert inspectors visually assess the resulting models, and each model is assigned the classification on which at least 75% of its inspectors agree. Of the 6073 grade A (secure) lens candidates, inspectors classify 4098 (67.5%) as successfully modelled, 580 (9.6%) as failures, 317 (5.2%) as multi-galaxy lenses, 15 (0.2%) as double-source-plane lenses, and 7 (0.1%) as unsure if lens, while 1032 (17.0%) reach no consensus and 24 (0.4%) have incomplete models. For the 8999 grade B (probable) candidates, the modelling success rate falls to 43.1%, primarily reflecting an increase in cases without consensus (37.6%), rather than a comparable increase in agreed failures (12.9%). Successfully modelled grade A and B systems have a median effective Einstein radius of 0.85 arcsec and a median total $I_E$-band source magnification of 8.1. We publicly release the successful lens models, their inferred properties, and magnified-source reconstructions through the ECLIPSE catalogue, demonstrating automated modelling at Euclid sample sizes and enabling population-level strong-lensing science.

figures.caption_en: Figure 1: Example results of automated preprocessing for the lens Euclid-DR1 J030313.592 \(-\) 580619.97. North is up and east is to the left, as in all images in this paper. Left : An RGB image using one colour scaling that contrasts the lens and source light with that of a nearby galaxy to the north-east. Right : An RGB image with different colour scaling that shows the fitting mask, candidate conjugate points, and contaminating-galaxy contour used in lens modelling. The white dashed circle shows the fitting mask, whose radius is computed from the furthest pixel in the segmented source emission, plus an additional buffer. White crosses with black outlines mark the automatically identified candidate conjugate points. The magenta contour marks a nearby contaminating galaxy whose light overlaps the fitting region and is therefore effectively excluded from the likelihood by zeroing its data values and inflating its RMS values.
figures.caption_zh: 图1：透镜Euclid-DR1 J030313.592 \(-\) 580619.97的自动化预处理示例结果。北向上，东向左，如本文所有图像所示。左：使用一种颜色缩放的RGB图像，将透镜和源的光与东北方向附近星系的光形成对比。右：使用不同颜色缩放的RGB图像，显示了透镜建模中使用的拟合掩膜、候选共轭点和污染星系轮廓。白色虚线圆显示拟合掩膜，其半径由分割源发射中最远像素计算得出，并加上额外缓冲。带有黑色轮廓的白色十字标记自动识别的候选共轭点。品红色轮廓标记附近的一个污染星系，其光与拟合区域重叠，因此通过将其数据值置零并增大其RMS值，有效地将其从似然中排除。

figures.caption_en: Figure 2: Example VIS PyAutoLens lens-model summary for the lens candidate J030313.592 \(-\) 580619.97, the same system shown in Fig. 1 . The top row shows, from left to right, the VIS data, the full model image, the signal-to-noise ratio map, and a maximally zoomed view of the reconstructed source plane. The middle row shows the foreground lens-light model, the lens-subtracted image, the lensed source model image, and a mid-zoom source-plane reconstruction. The bottom row shows the normalised residual map, the same residual map plotted in the range from \(-1\sigma\) to \(+1\sigma\) , the \(\chi^{2}\) map, and the full source-plane reconstruction. figures.caption_en: Figure 6: Two outcomes of the Double Source Plane Lens (DSPL) classification. Panels follow the same layout as Fig. 3 . The top row shows a genuine DSPL that inspectors correctly identified. Whilst the RGB image already provides strong visual evidence for multiple lensed sources, the poor lens-model fit resulting from the violation of the single-source-plane assumption provides an additional diagnostic that the system is a DSPL. The bottom row shows a grade A candidate receiving \(4/5\) ( \(80\%\) ) DSPL votes. The additional blue feature south of (below) the lens may have motivated the DSPL classification, but its nature is uncertain: it could be associated with the main lensed source, a second lensed source, or an unrelated line-of-sight object. Visual agreement alone therefore does not establish the presence of two lensed sources at distinct redshifts.
figures.caption_zh: 图6：双源平面透镜（DSPL）分类的两种结果。面板布局与图3相同。顶行显示检查员正确识别的真实DSPL。虽然RGB图像已经为多个透镜化源提供了强烈的视觉证据，但违反单源平面假设导致的透镜模型拟合不佳提供了额外的诊断，表明该系统是DSPL。底行显示一个A级候选体，获得\(4/5\)（\(80\%\)）的DSPL投票。透镜以南（下方）的额外蓝色特征可能促使了DSPL分类，但其性质不确定：它可能与主透镜化源、第二个透镜化源或无关的视线物体有关。因此，仅凭视觉一致性不能确定存在两个不同红移的透镜化源。

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
comment: 23 pages, 13 figures, submitted to A&A. Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"
summary: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 我们介绍了在Euclid数据发布1（DR1）中识别$15\,000$个高质量星系-星系强透镜候选体所采用的方法。鉴于透镜本质上是稀有系统，而DR1数据集规模庞大，本次透镜搜索分多个阶段进行：目录级筛选；机器学习和集成搜索；两阶段公民科学搜索；最后由强透镜研究人员对透镜候选体进行分级。在本文中，我们描述了每个搜索阶段及其各自的结果。本次搜索得益于神经网络对超过6800万个天体的自动分类、公民科学家志愿者对$300\,000$个天体的超过450万次分类，以及强透镜研究人员对超过$30\,000$个天体的检查。我们发现这种多阶段方法有助于最大化识别出的透镜数量，同时最小化公民科学家和强透镜研究人员的检查需求。我们在全面搜索中测得对A级（‘确定’）系统的完备度为$0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$，对A+B级（‘确定’+‘可能’）系统的完备度为$0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$。因此，我们的搜索识别了DR1区域内大多数确定的强透镜系统，其余可能是更暗或更模糊的情况。我们发现研究者分级仍然主观；在这项工作中，我们实施了校准以考虑个体检查者的偏差，并强调了透镜建模（ECLIPSE-C）在确定透镜候选体性质方面的益处。本文是ECLIPSE系列的一部分，这里聚焦于用于识别Euclid DR1中透镜候选体的发现流程；所发现透镜的概述见ECLIPSE-A。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 该多阶段策略在最大化识别透镜数量的同时，降低了公民科学家与研究者的检查负担；搜索能识别DR1区域内多数确定的强透镜系统，其余可能为更暗或更模糊的情形。研究者分级仍具主观性，需校准偏差，透镜建模有助于判定候选体性质。本文属于ECLIPSE系列，聚焦DR1发现流程，透镜总览见ECLIPSE-A。（基于可用摘要）

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) A: Strong lens catalogue overview
comment: 28 pages. Submitted to A&A as part of the Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release"
summary: We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.

AI.tldr: Euclid DR1 中发布 15072 个高置信度强引力透镜候选体（6073 个 A 级、8999 个 B 级），另加 9010 个 C 级候选，并给出自动透镜模型、测光红移与恒星族参数。
AI.motivation: 强引力透镜此前多为零星发现，样本小、非同质且多为地面低分辨率成像，难以作为统计工具使用；Euclid 高分辨率宽视场成像有望把该领域转变为可靠的统计与宇宙学探针。

artifacts.abstract_zh: 我们在Euclid数据发布1（DR1）中呈现了15072个高置信度强透镜候选体，覆盖2000 deg$^2$。其中包括6073个A级（“确定透镜”）和8999个B级（“可能透镜”）系统，并与另外9010个C级（“潜在透镜”）候选体一同发布。该样本的高置信度候选体数量超过以往所有星表的总和，建立了一个大规模、同质的星系尺度强透镜数据集，并具有高分辨率成像，将强透镜从罕见发现领域转变为天体物理和宇宙学的稳健统计工具。在DR1中约9亿个源中，我们使用定制的发现流程搜索了通过星表选择的6800万个源，该流程综合了五个机器学习模型的评分以及约7000名公民科学家和67名强透镜专家的视觉分类。除经典爱因斯坦环外，我们的星表还包括84个候选双源面透镜和超过1000个候选盘状透镜，这两类奇异类别此前已知例子很少，以及数百个候选透镜化AGN和类星体。我们为合并的A+B级系统提供自动透镜模型，并为偏转体星系提供测光红移和恒星族性质，提供可直接用于科学的数据产品。我们发现大多数偏转体星系是大质量且宁静的，恒星质量为$\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$（Salpeter初始质量函数；第16-84百分位范围）。偏转体星系覆盖一定范围的测光红移（$z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$），延伸至比以往地面透镜样本更高的红移，透镜的典型爱因斯坦半径为$0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec。按面积外推，我们预期在Euclid宽巡天中拥有超过100000个高置信度强透镜候选体。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 该工作建立了大样本、同质、高分辨率且可直接用于科学分析的星系级强透镜数据集，偏转体红移分布较以往地面样本更高；按面积外推，Euclid 宽巡天预期可获逾 10 万个高置信度强透镜候选。

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) D: Photometric redshifts and the first census of strong lenses in the galaxy evolution framework
comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release''
summary: The Euclid mission is revolutionising the study of strong gravitational lenses by providing high-resolution imaging over an unprecedented survey area, increasing the number of known lenses by two orders of magnitude compared to previous surveys. Characterising this sample of lens-galaxies requires accurate measurements of their physical properties. However, standard catalogue photometry often blends the light from the foreground lens and the lensed background source, limiting the reliability of derived galaxy parameters. We present a homogeneous catalogue of photometric redshifts and physical properties for 9538 galaxy-scale strong lenses identified in Euclid's DR1 strong-lens sample. We use deblended multiwavelength photometry obtained from the lens modelling of Euclid and ground-based images with PyAutoLens. The photometric redshifts of the lens galaxies are estimated using the template-fitting code Phosphoros. The stellar masses, SFRs, stellar ages, and metallicities are inferred through SED fitting with Prospector, adopting a flexible non-parametric SFH and a Salpeter IMF. The robustness of the inferred parameters is assessed through comparisons with spectroscopic redshifts and external galaxy surveys. The sample of lenses spans a broad redshift range of $0.13\lesssim z_{\rm phot} \lesssim 1.98$, with a median $z_{\rm phot} = 0.68^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$. The sample is dominated by massive quiescent galaxies with a $M_\ast$ range $[10^{10},\,10^{12.1}]\,M_\odot$ and a median $\log_{10}(M_\ast/M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$. This catalogue represents one of the first large-scale characterisations of strong-lens galaxies in the Euclid era. By combining deblended photometry with homogeneous photometric redshift and SED-fitting analyses, it provides a foundation for studies of galaxy evolution, lens-galaxy scaling relations, and the connection between stellar and total mass in strong lenses.

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NISP spectroscopy of gravitational arcs and multiple images
comment: Paper intended for the A&A Special Issue "Euclid First Data Release". 15 pages, 5 figures
summary: Applications of strong gravitational lensing in astrophysics and cosmology critically depend on building reliable strong lensing models, which require accurate measurements of on-sky positions of multiple images and of the redshifts of the background sources from which they originate. In this context, Euclid is a unique facility, as it simultaneously provides high-resolution multi-band photometric imaging and slitless spectroscopy for an unprecedentedly large sample of gravitational lenses, most of which are newly discovered. In this work, we exploit Euclid slitless spectroscopic data to determine the redshifts of four spatially extended lensed sources, and to reconstruct emission-line images. Specifically, two of the target sources are lensed into giant arcs by the massive galaxy clusters SPT-CLJ0411$-$4819 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.424$, where "d" denotes the lensing deflector) and Abell 2280 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.326$). The third system is a quadruply imaged active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidate strongly lensed by a massive galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.68$, while the fourth is a galaxy-scale Einstein ring produced by a lens galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.235$. This work represents a proof of concept for the exploitation of Euclid slitless spectroscopic data in the study of strong gravitational lensing, providing one of the first determinations of spectroscopic redshifts for strongly lensed features from NISP spectra. These results demonstrate the feasibility of applying the same methodology to the very large sample of gravitational lenses that Euclid has started to discover and is expected to identify over the course of the mission.

title: Prospects for probing supermassive binary black holes in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei via microlensing effects
summary: Gravitational microlensing in strongly lensed active galactic nuclei (AGNs) provides a powerful probe of accretion-disk structure and may offer a unique opportunity to identify sub-parsec supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) through distinctive signatures. Upcoming wide-field surveys are expected to discover a large sample of strongly lensed AGNs, a fraction of which may host SMBBHs detectable via microlensing. In this paper, we employ semi-analytic models to assess the detection prospects of sub-parsec SMBBHs in lensed AGNs, focusing on systems with resolvable multiple images suitable for microlensing analysis. Accounting for galaxy-scale strong-lensing statistics, and including the cluster-lensing contribution as an optimistic statistical extension, we estimate that up to approximately 87 such systems could be spatially resolved by individual upcoming surveys, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Rubin), Euclid, China's Space Survey Telescope (CSST), and the Roman. For the Rubin WFD survey, we estimate that periodic oscillations in microlensing light curves could identify $\sim0.12-0.68$ short-period ($<5$\,yr) binaries, whereas diagnostics based on the reconstructed size-wavelength relation apply to a broader population, potentially identifying $\sim0.4-5.3$ systems, depending on the model assumptions. CSST, Euclid, and Roman may also reveal up to $10.6$, $8.9$, and $1.2$ systems exhibiting size-wavelength features, and $2.3$, $1.9$, $0.3$ systems showing periodic oscillations, which should be regarded as imaging-selected candidates whose microlensing-based identification requires adequate time-domain follow-up, including cadence, monitoring baseline, photometric precision, and reliable time-delay measurements. Our results show that strongly lensed AGNs provide a promising, though observationally demanding, pathway for finding candidate SMBBHs via microlensing.

title: The PAU Survey: Dissecting strong-lensing systems with narrow-band photometric redshifts
summary: Wide-field imaging surveys such as Euclid will identify large samples of strong-lens candidates, whose scientific use requires redshifts for both deflectors and lensed sources. Source redshifts are challenging because faint arcs are blended with foreground light. We test lens-model-informed photometry on eight known strong lenses, using broad-band models to define component regions, point-reflection subtraction to reduce contamination, and PAU Survey narrow bands combined with five HSC or CFHT broad bands. BCNz estimates separate lens and source redshift distributions without imposing their expected ordering. All eight lens redshift peaks agree with spectroscopy within $|δ_z|\leq0.014$, where $δ_z=(z_b-z_{\rm spec})/(1+z_{\rm spec})$. Four source peaks, all at $z_{\rm s}^{\rm spec}\leq1.23$, agree within $|δ_z|\leq0.025$. Symmetric subtraction reduces the median source $|δ_z|$ from 0.336 to 0.071. At $|δ_z|<0.05$, narrow- plus broad-band photometry yields eight lens and four source matches, versus three and two using EAZY with broad bands alone. These results demonstrate component redshift recovery in blended systems and support redshift-based lens-candidate assessment alongside morphology and colour. Larger narrow-band surveys, including J-PAS, could extend this approach, pending uncertainty calibration and blind candidate tests.

title: VENUS: Strong Lens Mass Models and Einstein Radii of 60 Galaxy Clusters
summary: We present the strong lens mass modeling result of 60 galaxy clusters targeted by Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) multi-epoch Treasury program. We obtain refined mass models for the 60 clusters with the glafic software by fitting positions of $\sim 4500$ multiple images, $\sim 1150$ of which are newly identified multiple images with help of multi-band JWST images. Each cluster contains typically $\sim 50$ multiple images, thanks to the selection of target clusters based on their high lensing strengths. We validate our models with the Jackknife method. The median Einstein radius is $\sim 30''$ and the distribution of the Einstein radii extends out to $\sim 60''$ for the source redshift of 9, which confirms that their lensing strengths are indeed among the highest known to date. For the source redshift of 9, we identify MACS J0717.5+3745, MACS J0600.1$-$2008, and PLCK G287.0+32.9 as clusters with the largest Einstein radii as well as the largest areas of the high-magnification ($|μ|>10$) regions. We find that the observed Einstein radii of VENUS clusters are fully compatible with the standard cold dark matter model.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 我们展示了由詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜（JWST）多历元财政部项目“新生未探索源大规模探索”（VENUS）所观测的60个星系团的强透镜质量建模结果。我们利用glafic软件，通过拟合约4500个多重像的位置，获得了这60个星系团的精细质量模型，其中约1150个多重像是借助JWST多波段图像新识别出的。由于目标星系团是基于其高透镜强度筛选的，每个星系团通常包含约50个多重像。我们采用Jackknife方法验证了模型。对于源红移为9的情况，爱因斯坦半径的中位数约为30角秒，且爱因斯坦半径分布延伸至约60角秒，这证实了它们的透镜强度确实属于迄今已知的最高之列。对于源红移为9，我们确定MACS J0717.5+3745、MACS J0600.1$-$2008和PLCK G287.0+32.9为具有最大爱因斯坦半径以及最大高放大率（$|\mu|>10$）区域面积的星系团。我们发现VENUS星系团观测到的爱因斯坦半径与标准冷暗物质模型完全一致。

title: Self-interacting Dark Matter signatures from stars extremely magnified by galaxy clusters
summary: The spatial distribution of cluster-lensed star transients with respect to the macroscopic critical curve (CC) is sensitive to underlying substructures predicted by different classes of dark matter (DM) models. \citet{Broadhurst_2025} have shown that wave-like DM composed of ultra-light bosons better explains both the width and negative skewness (towards the interior of the CC) of the lensed star spatial distribution discovered in the ``Dragon'' lensed galaxy ($z = 0.73$) in the Abell 370 (A370, $z = 0.375$) cluster field, compared with the case of regular cold dark matter (CDM) subhaloes. In this work, we consider the case of self-interacting DM (SIDM) and investigate how the lensed star spatial distribution depends on the velocity-dependent self-interaction cross-section of SIDM particles, and whether constraints can be placed on the cross-section strength at relevant velocities. Establishing a cross-section strength-dependent (sub)halo gravothermal core-collapse probability, we found that the SIDM appears to be the only known class of models thus far in which the sign of skewness is set by its own particle parameters. The observed lensed star distribution in the Dragon galaxy can be well explained, in terms of both skewness and width, when a significant fraction of subhaloes have undergone core collapse and exhibit a steep power-law density slope. Given the cluster redshift, this qualitatively favours an (effective) cross-section strength of $500 -1000\,\textrm{cm}^{2}/\textrm{g}$ for halos with mass $10^{6} - 10^{8}\,M_{\odot}$ (velocity dispersion of $\sim 1-10\,\rm{km}/\rm{s}$), when the role of environmental effects on the core-collapse (de)acceleration is not considered, and limits the three-dimensional inner density slope of the collapsed halo to $Γ\gtrsim 2.5$ (Bayes factor of $\sim 10^{2}$).

AI.tldr: 本文研究自相互作用暗物质（SIDM）情形下，Dragon 星系团透镜恒星的空间分布如何依赖速度相关的自相互作用截面，并据此对截面强度和塌缩晕的内密度斜率给出约束。
AI.motivation: 不同暗物质模型预言的子结构会改变簇透镜恒星相对宏观临界线（CC）的空间分布形态，已有工作表明波状超轻玻色子暗物质比CDM子晕更好地解释Dragon星系（z=0.73，位于Abell 370场中）中观测到的分布宽度和负偏度（偏向CC内侧）。作者希望检验SIDM是否也能解释该观测，并能否由此约束截面。
AI.method: 建立依赖于自相互作用截面强度的（子）晕引力热核心塌缩概率模型，计算塌缩晕具有陡幂律密度剖面时的透镜恒星空间分布，并与观测的偏度和宽度比较，同时用贝叶斯因子评估内密度斜率的下限。

title: CosmoSim: Lens-parameter estimation of the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 using machine learning
summary: CosmoSim is an open-source tool for simulating gravitational lenses and reconstructing lens mass distributions, either by ray tracing a parametric lens model or through a Roulette expansion of the lens potential. It is also used to generate the large, labelled synthetic image sets needed to train machine-learning (ML) parameter estimators. We present the first application of CosmoSim to real data. A convolutional neural network trained only on CosmoSim images estimates Singular Isothermal Ellipsoid lens and source parameters directly from observed images. We test the pipeline on 21 images of 19 strong lenses from Euclid and the AGEL survey, after removing the foreground lens light with a custom decontamination tool built on AstroPy. As a case study we reconstruct the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 both from the lens model published by the discovery team and from parameters predicted by our ML model. Both reconstructions recover the observed four-image structure, and the ML-based reconstruction performs at least as well as the literature-based one: it scores better on masked structural similarity, intersection-over-union and Chamfer distance, with an essentially equal Hausdorff distance. Across the ensemble, the predicted Einstein radii are consistent with catalogued values within the quoted uncertainties (mean relative difference 0.08 for Euclid and 0.19 for AGEL lenses), and the enclosed masses agree to within a median of 0.12 dex. The predicted ellipticities differ systematically from the catalogued values, while the comparison of orientations is inconclusive. These results establish CosmoSim as a tool that can be applied directly to observational data.

AI.tldr: CosmoSim模拟管线首次直接应用于真实观测数据：仅用其生成图像训练的卷积神经网络，可从Euclid与AGEL巡天的强透镜观测图像中估计SIE透镜与源参数，并在NGC 6505上取得与文献模型相当甚至更优的重建效果。
AI.motivation: CosmoSim是开源引力透镜模拟与质量分布重建工具，也可生成带标签的合成图像集用于训练机器学习参数估计器，但此前缺少在真实观测数据上的验证，作者希望检验该模拟管线能否直接迁移到实际观测（含前景透镜光干扰）场景。
AI.method: 使用仅在CosmoSim合成图像上训练的卷积神经网络，直接从观测图像估计奇异等温椭球（SIE）透镜参数与源参数；在19个强透镜的21幅图像（来自Euclid和AGEL巡天）上测试，测试前用基于AstroPy自研的去污染工具去除前景透镜光；并以爱因斯坦十字NGC 6505为案例，分别基于文献参数与ML预测参数进行重建对比。
AI.result: NGC 6505的两种重建均再现四像结构，ML重建在掩膜结构相似度、交并比、Chamfer距离上优于文献模型，Hausdorff距离基本相当；整体样本中预测爱因斯坦半径与星表值在误差范围内一致（平均相对偏差Euclid 0.08、AGEL 0.19），所围质量中位偏差0.12 dex；预测椭率与星表值存在系统性差异，取向比较无定论。
AI.conclusion: 结果表明CosmoSim可作为可直接应用于真实观测数据的工具，其合成数据训练的ML估计器在真实强透镜图像上具有良好参数恢复能力，但在椭率与取向等形态参数上仍有待改进。

artifacts.abstract_zh: CosmoSim 是一个开源工具，用于模拟引力透镜并重建透镜质量分布，既可以通过对参数化透镜模型进行光线追踪，也可以通过透镜势的 Roulette 展开来实现。它还被用于生成训练机器学习（ML）参数估计器所需的大型带标签合成图像集。我们展示了 CosmoSim 首次应用于真实数据。一个仅在 CosmoSim 图像上训练的卷积神经网络直接从观测图像中估计奇异等温椭球透镜和源参数。我们在来自 Euclid 和 AGEL 巡天的 19 个强透镜的 21 幅图像上测试了该流程，此前使用基于 AstroPy 构建的自定义去污染工具移除了前景透镜光。作为案例研究，我们分别从发现团队发表的透镜模型和我们的 ML 模型预测的参数重建了爱因斯坦十字 NGC 6505。两种重建均恢复了观测到的四像结构，且基于 ML 的重建表现至少与基于文献的重建相当：它在掩膜结构相似性、交并比和 Chamfer 距离上得分更高，而 Hausdorff 距离基本相等。在整个样本中，预测的爱因斯坦半径与目录值在所述不确定度内一致（Euclid 透镜的平均相对差异为 0.08，AGEL 透镜为 0.19），所包含的质量在 0.12 dex 的中位数范围内一致。预测的椭率与目录值存在系统性差异，而取向的比较尚无定论。这些结果确立了 CosmoSim 作为可直接应用于观测数据的工具的地位。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 基于可用摘要：结果表明 CosmoSim 可作为可直接应用于真实观测数据的工具，其合成数据训练的 ML 估计器在真实强透镜图像上具有良好参数恢复能力，但在椭率与取向等形态参数上仍有待改进。
